explanation: I found no Mathlib declaration that states this result. I didn't search Mathlib; I judged from the statement and its proof alone. Every constant in the statement belongs to the library: `zigzagProjectiveMiddleEquivNeighborHeads`, `zigzagProjectiveHeadEquivSocle`, `zigzagBasis`, `zigzagVolume`, `nonisolatedZigzagQuotient`, and the radical-power notation `R`. The lemma just evaluates one of the library's own linear equivalences on a quotient class. The proof unfolds the definition and runs `simp` with general Mathlib lemmas (`LinearEquiv.trans_apply`, `Submodule.quotEquivOfEq_mk`, `LinearMap.quotKerEquivOfSurjective_apply_mk`, `LinearEquiv.piCongrRight_apply`) and with the library's own lemmas (`middleToSocles_apply`, `coe_radical_smul`, `coe_socleVector`). Those Mathlib lemmas are generic API that doesn't count here, so the mathematical content sits in the library's definitions and Mathlib has no counterpart.
